what_it_counts: people with conviction records estimated eligible for sealing under current law who have not received it (conviction 'second chance gap')
source_title: The Colorado Second Chance Sealing Gap (Paper Prisons Initiative)
notes: Published as '~873K'. Also '~1.4M people with any records that are eligible for relief but haven't received it'. 94.5% = 'remaining ... in Colorado's second chance sealing gap' (uptake ~5.5%), stated for people with any records. Report undated; latest data year 2019, cites law effective Sept 2021; year approximate. A 2022 update on the proposed Clean Slate bill also exists.

source_title: The Delaware Second Chance Expungement Gap (Paper Prisons Initiative)

source_title: The Illinois Second Chance Expungement and Sealing Gap (Paper Prisons Initiative)
notes: Published as '~921K'. Also ~2.2M people with criminal records eligible for any relief (not explicitly stated as un-relieved). 90% of eligible people with conviction records in the gap (uptake ~10%). Uses 2021 sealing data; report undated, year approximate.

what_it_counts: people with conviction records estimated eligible for sealing/expungement under current law who have not received it (conviction 'second chance gap')
source_title: The Kentucky Second Chance Expungement Gap (Paper Prisons Initiative)
notes: Key findings table: '~1.1M' (91% of ~1.2M with conviction records); the abstract text on the same page says '1.2M people with conviction records that are eligible' - internal inconsistency. Also ~1.4M with any record eligible. 96% left in the gap (uptake ~4.0%). PDF created March 2023.

notes: Published as '1M+' / '~1M+'. 97% of eligible people with conviction records in the gap (uptake 3%); abstract also says '97-99% second chance gap'. 58% of eligible owe fines/fees. Year approximate (mentions COVID 2020-21).
